subject: trio-ethnography in programming education
object: interpretive reflective approach for understanding AI-supported learning
statement: The paper proposes trio-ethnography as a valuable reflective approach for helping computing educators move beyond observable student behaviors toward a richer understanding of AI-supported learning.

subject: student learning visibility
object: invisible classroom learning processes revealed via student narratives
statement: The paper shows that student narratives revealed learning processes that were largely invisible in the classroom, prompting educators to reconsider assumptions about AI use, assessment, and programming instruction.

subject: TRACE-Router routing framework
object: improved accuracy-latency trade-off on agentic benchmarks
statement: The paper reports that TRACE-Router consistently improves the accuracy-latency trade-off, achieving non-dominated Pareto frontier points across three agentic benchmarks.

subject: TRACE-Router on tau2-Bench
object: 7-8 point accuracy gain over latency-matched interpolation
statement: The paper reports 7-8 accuracy points improvement over latency-matched interpolation between individual models on tau2-Bench.

subject: TRACE-Router on Terminal-Bench
object: 7.1 point accuracy gain with 36% lower latency
statement: The paper reports 7.1 higher accuracy points than the strongest single model baseline with 36% lower latency on Terminal-Bench.

subject: generalization bound for solver iterates
object: Rademacher complexity bound with k-neighborhood analysis
statement: The paper derives a generalization bound based on Rademacher complexity that reveals the role of k-neighborhoods and related parameters in learning projected gradient descent solver iterates.

subject: k-neighborhood data collection
object: augmented training data from intermediate solver iterates
statement: The paper proposes a k-neighborhood data collection strategy that augments datasets of converged solutions with intermediate solver iterates, increasing the amount of training data without additional solver runs.

subject: ADAPT-GQE quantum circuit synthesis
object: generative AI framework for ground-state preparation
statement: The paper introduces ADAPT-GQE, a generative AI framework that learns to synthesize ground-state preparation circuits for electronic structure calculations using transformer models trained on ADAPT-VQE reference circuits.

subject: ADAPT-GQE performance
object: order-of-magnitude circuit generation speedup
statement: The paper reports that ADAPT-GQE achieves order-of-magnitude reductions in circuit generation time relative to ADAPT-VQE while maintaining comparable or improved state-preparation accuracy.

subject: ADAPT-GQE execution on quantum hardware
object: AI-generated circuits executed on Quantinuum Helios-1
statement: The paper reports executing ADAPT-GQE-generated circuits on Quantinuum Helios-1 quantum hardware, representing a milestone for AI-generated quantum chemistry circuits on state-of-the-art hardware.

subject: MineValiCoder on HumanEval
object: 96.34% Pass@1 score on HumanEval
statement: The paper reports MineValiCoder achieves Pass@1 score of 96.34% on HumanEval.

subject: MineValiCoder on MBPP
object: 87.40% Pass@1 score on MBPP
statement: The paper reports MineValiCoder achieves Pass@1 score of 87.40% on MBPP.

subject: MineValiCoder on APPS
object: 64.00% Pass@1 score on APPS
statement: The paper reports MineValiCoder achieves Pass@1 score of 64.00% on APPS.

subject: MineValiCoder on LiveCodeBench
object: 51.33% Pass@1 score on LiveCodeBench
statement: The paper reports MineValiCoder achieves Pass@1 score of 51.33% on LiveCodeBench.

subject: MineValiCoder framework
object: collaborative TDD framework with test quality mining
statement: The paper proposes MineValiCoder, a collaborative closed-loop Test-Driven Development framework that addresses LLM stochasticity through test case quality mining and bipartite graph-based mutual validation.

subject: negative-shifted gradient descent
object: mixed-sign spectral regularization escaping negative ridge
statement: The paper proposes early-stopped negative-shifted gradient descent that escapes constraints of stable negative-ridge endpoints, enabling mixed-sign-capable filtering for spectral regularization.

subject: Marchenko-Pastur barrier in ridge regression
object: bulk-width shift canceling implicit penalty
statement: The paper shows that in a Gaussian spike-plus-flat model, there exists a Marchenko-Pastur barrier where the shift canceling the implicit penalty lies a bulk width above the smallest empirical eigenvalue.

subject: legal nugget extraction
object: nugget-based retrieval for jurisprudential collections
statement: The paper proposes a pipeline that extracts legal nuggets (short self-contained legal theses) from documents, indexes them with embeddings, retrieves nugget-level evidence, and aggregates to document-level rankings.

subject: nugget retrieval on JUA-Juris
object: NDCG@10 increases from 0.10265 to 0.20461
statement: The paper reports that nugget retrieval substantially improves jurisprudential search, with NDCG@10 increasing from 0.10265 to 0.20461 on JUA-Juris.

subject: nugget retrieval on JurisTCU
object: NDCG@10 increases from 0.20898 to 0.32696
statement: The paper reports NDCG@10 increasing from 0.20898 to 0.32696 on JurisTCU with nugget retrieval.

subject: SVD soft-thresholding via polar decomposition
object: significant GPU speedup using polar decomposition
statement: The paper reports that singular value soft-thresholding computed via reduction to matrix polar decomposition exhibits significant speed-up on GPUs compared to the standard approach using SVD.

subject: LoRA condition number analysis
object: small condition numbers contribute marginally to adaptation
statement: The paper shows for the first time that LoRA matrices with smaller condition numbers are already well-balanced across directions and contribute only marginally to adaptation.

subject: kappa-LoRA method
object: selective LoRA fine-tuning by condition number ranking
statement: The paper proposes kappa-LoRA, which optimizes LoRA by focusing updates on matrices with the largest condition numbers, restricting updates to the top 50% of weight matrices ranked by condition number.

subject: kappa-LoRA efficiency gains
object: 16.2% faster fine-tuning with 4.5% memory reduction
statement: The paper reports kappa-LoRA cuts fine-tuning time by 16.2% on average while matching the accuracy of standard LoRA and reducing memory cost by 4.5%.

subject: PRO-clinical dysphagia prediction
object: two-stage stacking for swallowing impairment risk
statement: The paper proposes a clinically interpretable two-stage stacking model to predict swallowing impairment risk using patient-reported outcome responses and structured clinical variables, without requiring videofluoroscopic imaging.

subject: MDADI item-level predictive information
object: individual responses beyond composite summary scores
statement: The paper shows that individual MDADI responses contain predictive information beyond that captured by composite or global summary scores in dysphagia risk assessment.

subject: regression in LLM agent skills
object: regressions dominate performance gains in best skills
statement: The paper shows that regressions are substantial enough that the best performing skills outperform others primarily by regressing less, not by gaining more, across nearly 6,000 runs on two office automation benchmarks.

subject: causes of LLM skill-induced regression
object: three modes of regression identified
statement: The paper identifies three causes of regression: (i) skill description osmosis (skill changes behavior by presence alone), (ii) grounding displacement (prescribed procedure overrides input interpretation), and (iii) verification displacement (procedure suppresses output checks).

subject: grounding and verification in skill reliability
object: reliability depends on grounding and verification
statement: The paper shows that after correcting evaluation artifacts, reliability depends more on grounding and verification than on procedural skill choice, with many regressions recoverable through better grounding and verification.

subject: RL for air traffic control decision-making
object: reinforcement learning agent for alternative route decisions
statement: The paper proposes training an intelligent agent with a reinforcement learning algorithm to make decisions on alternative flight routes that avoid no-fly zones in air traffic control.

subject: saliency map explainability for ATC RL
object: saliency maps for RL decision interpretability
statement: The paper employs saliency maps as a preliminary explainability approach, providing insights into the input features that most significantly influence the agent's decision-making process in ATC.

subject: Skill Self-Play co-evolutionary framework
object: proposer-solver-controller co-evolution loop
statement: The paper introduces Skill Self-Play (Skill-SP), a co-evolutionary framework comprising a proposer (generates tasks conditioned on skills), a solver (explores solutions), and a dynamic skill controller, orchestrated via a reinforcement learning loop.

subject: Skill-SP performance improvements
object: consistently pushes performance ceiling of models
statement: The paper reports Skill-SP, serving as a robust evolution engine, consistently pushes the performance ceiling of competent backbones while catalyzing striking turnarounds for initially misaligned models on tool-use and reasoning benchmarks.

subject: SM4RT Structured Motion Transformer
object: structured 4D reconstruction from monocular RGB video
statement: The paper proposes SM4RT, a Structured Motion 4D Reconstruction Transformer for end-to-end 3D reconstruction and structured motion perception from monocular RGB video.

subject: Structure-of-Motion decomposition
object: motion bases decomposed into 6D SE(3) twists
statement: The paper introduces Structure-of-Motion to represent scene dynamics, where scene motion is decomposed into a compact set of motion bases each represented as temporal sequences of 6D twists in SE(3).

subject: SM4RT motion reconstruction
object: strong motion reconstruction with geometric structure
statement: The paper shows SM4RT achieves strong motion reconstruction performance while preserving the geometric structure of scene motion, recovering rigid-body motion trajectories for objects.
